body.heading: Set the stage, not the mood
paragraphs: Homework friction often starts before the homework does: a hungry child, an unclear start time, a screen switched off mid-game. A small routine — snack first, same start time, same place, phone in another room — removes the negotiations that wear everyone down.

Agree the order with the child, not for them: what comes first, how long a stretch lasts, when the break is. A plan they helped make is a plan they can be reminded of without it feeling like an ambush.

body.heading: Be a lamp, not a helicopter
paragraphs: Sit nearby with your own book or work if company helps, and be available for questions — but let the work stay theirs. Struggling briefly with a hard sum is not a problem to rescue them from; it is the learning happening.

If the same battle repeats daily over the same subject, that is information, not defiance. A word with the teacher, earlier and kinder than you think necessary, usually helps more than another evening of pressure.

body.heading: End on time
paragraphs: When the agreed time is up, homework closes — finished or not — and the evening returns to the family. A clear end protects both the work and the relationship, and teaches that effort is measured in honest time, not in tears.
Protect one homework-free stretch of the evening for everyone, parents included. A family that stops working at a civilised hour teaches more about work than any lecture.

description: A snack, a fixed start, company without hovering, and an end time: homework as a routine instead of a nightly negotiation.
